name: Haldex Generation 5 AWD coupling controller (MQB)

read_methods.notes: No public read/flash procedure found. The controller plug carries terminals 15 and 30, ground and a dedicated Haldex CAN pair (OpenHaldex).

notes: Fifth-generation Haldex on MQB AWD cars (pump/kit part prefix 0CQ). OpenTune's haldex checksum (per-block 16-bit word-sum) is synthetic/vector-validated only. These are the pins of the in-line harness plug that mates with the Haldex controller, as documented by the OpenHaldex project (single source).

bench.notes: Terminal 30 on 3, terminal 15 on 1, ground 2, Haldex CAN-H 6 / CAN-L 5 (OpenHaldex).
bench.resistor_notes: Termination of the Haldex CAN segment is not documented; measure the resistance between CAN-H and CAN-L on the unit first.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
